findings.R01: Each distinct subskill has its own focused set; the subskill matrix is rebuilt from the actual question mapping (splits S1/S97/S98, S2/S99, S7/S100, S24/S101, S28/S102, S75/S103, S77/S104, S87/S105)
findings.R02: All five MAIN questions are comparable full performances: proofs in proof sets, constructions with evidence in construction sets, derivations or informal arguments in derive/explain sets; true/false items removed from every MAIN
findings.R03: Forward branches audited for focus and one new demand; duplicated or off-demand forward items replaced (S4-F2, S12-F1-Q4, S29-F1, S34-F1, S73-F1, S100-F2-Q3, and others)
findings.R04: Every question states its own givens (points on sides, right angles, tangency, heights, radii, models) instead of relying on a figure or an earlier question
findings.R05: No circular dependencies: SSS (S16) is justified with SAS and an angle bisector, not the perpendicular-bisector converse; S18 establishes corresponding angles by a translation before the other angle-pair theorems

findings.R10: S37 dilation items about lines use scale factors k ≠ 1
findings.R11: S38-F1-Q3 restricts to points other than the center and a dilation with k ≠ 1
findings.R12: Rotation items require P ≠ center (S8-M-Q4) and a point P different from the center O (S82-B1-Q1)
findings.R14: Domain assumptions stated: a > 0 and c ≠ 0 (S22-M-Q4, S67-F1-Q2), a ≠ 0 (S22-B2-Q2), P ≠ M (S14-F1-Q2), nonzero values before reciprocals (S42-B3-Q1)

findings.R19: S66-F1-Q3 uses |p| for the focus-vertex distance
findings.R20: S73-B2-Q4 uses the absolute value of the difference
findings.R21: S82-F2 rotation axes are in the rectangle's plane, parallel to a side, and outside the rectangle
findings.R22: S83-F2-Q1 key is 1,380 kg (2.3 m³ × 600 kg/m³)
findings.R23: S84-F2-Q2 asks for the smallest whole number of m² that meets the limit (3,334)
findings.R24: S87-F2-Q2 gives a baseline (a standard metal that never fails) and asks when the expected cost is strictly lower
findings.R25: S77-M-Q1 requires the general pyramid argument (vertical scaling and Cavalieri's principle), not only the cube dissection
findings.R26: Altitude derivations cover acute and obtuse cases (S88-M-Q1, S88-M-Q5, S89-M-Q3/Q5, S89-B1-Q2, S90-M-Q3)

findings.R30: S33-B3-Q5 says the point is not on the line
